after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic sine function is given by

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}\,\text{d}x=\sqrt{2}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}\,\text{d}x=\sqrt{2}\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

a
ln⁡|x|−4arcosh⁡x+C
b
ln⁡|x|−4artanh⁡x+C
c

decision.explanation: Integrate term by term: ∫1/x dx = ln|x| and ∫1/√(x²+1) dx = arsinh(x). Thus the result is ln|x|−4 arsinh(x)+C, option c.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic sine function is given by

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{x}-\frac{4}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}})\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x-4\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|-4\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2

∫(1x−4x2+1)dx=

a
ln⁡|x|−4arcosh⁡x+C
b
ln⁡|x|−4artanh⁡x+C
c
ln⁡|x|−4arsinh⁡x+C
d
4ln⁡|x−arsinh⁡x|+C
e
4ln⁡|x−arcosh⁡x|+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic sine function is given by ddx(arsinh⁡x)=1x2+1.

Therefore, we have

∫(1x−4x2+1)dx=∫1xdx−4∫1x2+1dx=ln⁡|x|−4arsinh⁡x+C.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option c. Differentiating ln|x|−4 arsinh(x)+C gives 1/x−4/√(x²+1), exactly the integrand for x≠0. The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option a.

content.worked_solution:
The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic sine function is given by

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{x}-\frac{4}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}})\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x-4\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|-4\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Factor out the constant √2+1. Since the derivative of arsinh(x) is 1/√(x²+1), the integral is (√2+1)arsinh(x)+C, option a.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic sine function is given by

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\sqrt{2}+1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}\,\text{d}x=(\sqrt{2}+1)\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}\,\text{d}x=(\sqrt{2}+1)\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

∫(4x2−1+sinh⁡x)dx=

a
4arcosh⁡x+tanh⁡x+C
b
−4arsinh⁡x+tanh⁡x+C
c
−4arcosh⁡x+cosh⁡x+C
d
4arcosh2⁡x+cosh⁡x+C
e
4arcosh⁡x+cosh⁡x+C
Submit

decision.explanation: For x>1, the derivative of arcosh(x) is 1/√(x²−1), and the derivative of cosh(x) is sinh(x). Integrating term by term gives option e.

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosine function is given by

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcosh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{4}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}+\operatorname{sinh}⁡x)\text{d}x & =4\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x+\int \operatorname{sinh}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\operatorname{arcosh}⁡x+\operatorname{cosh}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{artanh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\operatorname{arsinh}⁡2}{2(1-{x}^{2})}\,\text{d}x=\frac{\operatorname{arsinh}⁡2}{2}\int \frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{\operatorname{arsinh}⁡2}{2}\,\operatorname{artanh}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 12
?

Calculate ∫e−ln⁡71−x2dx for |x|<1.

a
eartanh⁡x−ln⁡7+C
b
(e−ln⁡7)arcoth⁡x+C
c
(ln⁡7−e)arsinh⁡x+C
d
(ln⁡7−e)artanh⁡x+C
e
(e−ln⁡7)artanh⁡x+C
Submit

decision.explanation: The numerator e−ln(7) is constant. Since d/dx artanh(x)=1/(1−x²) for |x|<1, the integral is (e−ln(7))artanh(x)+C, option e.

after.name: Question 12
after.worked_solution:
The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic tangent function is given by

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{artanh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{e-\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{1-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=(e-\operatorname{ln}⁡7)\int \frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=(e-\operatorname{ln}⁡7)\operatorname{artanh}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Calculate ∫e−ln⁡71−x2dx for |x|<1.

a
eartanh⁡x−ln⁡7+C
b
(e−ln⁡7)arcoth⁡x+C
c
(ln⁡7−e)arsinh⁡x+C
d
(ln⁡7−e)artanh⁡x+C
e
(e−ln⁡7)artanh⁡x+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic tangent function is given by ddx(artanh⁡x)=11−x2.

Therefore, we have

∫e−ln⁡71−x2dx=(e−ln⁡7)∫11−x2dx=(e−ln⁡7)artanh⁡x+C.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option e. Differentiating (e−ln(7))artanh(x)+C gives (e−ln(7))/(1−x²) for |x|<1. The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option d, whose coefficient has the opposite sign.

content.worked_solution:
The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic tangent function is given by

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{artanh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{e-\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{1-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=(e-\operatorname{ln}⁡7)\int \frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=(e-\operatorname{ln}⁡7)\operatorname{artanh}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 14
?

Calculate ∫(ex−6ln⁡5(1−x2))dx for |x|<1.

a
ex−6ln⁡5arsinh⁡x+C
b
ex−6artanh⁡x5+C
c
ex−6ln⁡5arcoth⁡x+C
d
ex−5artanh⁡5x+C
e
ex−6ln⁡5artanh⁡x+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integrating e^x gives e^x. Since artanh(x) has derivative 1/(1−x²) for |x|<1, the other term integrates to −(6/ln(5))artanh(x). This matches option e.

after.name: Question 14
after.worked_solution:
The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic tangent function is given by

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{artanh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({e}^{x}-\frac{6}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5(1-{x}^{2})})\text{d}x & =\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x-\frac{6}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\int \frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{x}-\frac{6}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\operatorname{artanh}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

−23arcosh⁡x+C

EXPLANATION

The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic tangent function is given by ddx(artanh⁡x)=11−x2.

Therefore, we have

∫23(1−x2)dx=23∫11−x2dx=23artanh⁡x+C.

content.worked_solution:
The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic tangent function is given by

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{artanh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\sqrt{2}}{3(1-{x}^{2})}\,\text{d}x=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\int \frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\operatorname{artanh}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
